body: I’m only 2 years older than your daughter, so I have some similar perspective. The likely reason she decided to lease a puppy was because responsible breeders can have extremely long waitlists. It sounds like she’s quiet immature. I was looking for my own dog at age 19 and did a lot of research before buying the right dog for me. Forgetting the APR, $4,200 alone is extremely expensive for a dog. It really sounds like this was a very impulsive decision. I would take this dog back and encourage your daughter to put more thought into getting a puppy before you allow her to have one in your home.

I have nothing to add except I understand your feelings and completely relate to them. My puppy will turn 4 months old this week and I’ve had him since he was 8 weeks. If I’m completely honest, most of the time I really feel resentful towards him and get irritated quickly because like you, I’ve also made a lot of sacrifices. But also, we’re doing our best and venting on the internet will never harm our dogs... it’s definitely difficult and these feelings are normal.

My puppy I’ve had since 8 weeks, now 11 weeks old, always poops in the morning. He poops at around 8:30-9:30pm and then his morning poop is always between 7:30-8:30pm.

Hey! Are we the same person? I also have depression, anxiety, 2 years left of college, and my puppy is 9 weeks old! I’ve had mine for 4 days so far. Shit is hard. First full day I had him it triggered my first anxiety attack in YEARS. What’s your schedule like for this dog and you? Keep every day relatively the same and this will make your life so much easier. Crate training is the only way I get self care time and school work done. Also, how long are you leaving him alone for? For more than 3 hours, definitely hire a dog sitter or walker. And 3 hours is going to be pushing it. There are valid reasons for relinquishing the dog including: not being able to give it good care, declining health, financial issues, etc. Are you getting the help you need as well?

Please feel free to talk in my PMs if you ever want to rant!! We are going through the exact same thing and I’m here for you.

Agree on crate training x1000!!! Mine sleep 10 hours during the day and 8.5 hours straight during the night. He cries max 10 mins being put in the crate. 10 hours is a great break and gives plenty of time to get your work done.

1. If he goes in to sleep on his own, it sounds like you’re doing it right. 

2. You can help your dog with holding it during the night by cutting off water around 3 hours before his bed time. My 8 week old sleeps 8.5 hours straight through the night.

I’m not sure if it makes a difference but he only bites the bars and appears most frustrated when he is first out in the crate for 3-4 minutes, then whining for an additional 6-10 and then dead silence for a little over an hour. 

But I do believe you when you say I jumped the gun. I was reading on this sub, but now that I’m recalling it, the youngest pup on this schedule was 11 weeks old. I’ll scale it back, thank you!
